notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), and no hardware was attached or run.

WHAT IT SERVES: the card's models[0], training/envs/go2_parkour_scene.xml, as a MujocoDriver in simulated mode R0. The scene has a floating-base Go2 with the root free joint at 0 0 0.42 (go2_parkour_scene.xml:23-24), twelve leg hinges, a five-joint arm and a two-finger gripper, and nineteen position actuators (go2_parkour_scene.xml:164-189). cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [...]}}; the bridge derives one control interval per actuator from the loaded model's actuator_ctrlrange, checks every element before writing data.ctrl, then mj_step runs ticks times. cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults with mj_resetData + mj_forward. The state is the bridge's integration state (time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed); the loaded model has 26 qpos, 25 qvel and 19 ctrl elements, and its option timestep is 0.005 s (go2_parkour_scene.xml:4).

WHY THIS SHAPE: the card's family-config/MujocoDriver decision matches the upstream, a MuJoCo/Gymnasium training environment for the Unitree Go2. The card's entry symbol training.envs.go2_mujoco_env:Go2MujocoEnv was confirmed at go2_mujoco_env.py:206; it loads the MJCF with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path (go2_mujoco_env.py:215-216), sets model.opt.timestep to SIM_DT (go2_mujoco_env.py:217) and calls mujoco.mj_step four times per policy step (go2_mujoco_env.py:871-873). The entry class points SCENE_XML at training/envs/go2_scene.xml (go2_mujoco_env.py:11), while this package serves the card's models[0], the parkour variant, following the MuJoCo playbook; both scenes carry the same robot, arm and actuator block. The difference is listed in the fidelity gaps. There is no DEVIATION FROM THE CARD in decision, helper or mode.

FAKE: MuJoCo is not installed and cannot be installed where the gate runs (no network, no pip), so backends['fake'] is this package's stand-in mujoco module in fake.py. It parses the served MJCF, resolves the MJCF default classes, and derives the nineteen actuator control ranges, the 26 qpos / 25 qvel dimensions and the option time step from the same text. Its integration is a placeholder joint motion at a placeholder rate, not MuJoCo's dynamics; it loads no mesh or height field, resolves no contact, equality or sensor constraint, and applies no damping, armature, gain or bias parameters. The real mujoco path (backend sim) was not run here. Every difference is in the driver's fidelity gaps.

WARNINGS (all expected, none failed): G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because backends['fake'] is the FakeMujoco class object (the stand-in mujoco namespace) rather than a '.fake:...' string, so the gate treats the fake as the upstream simulator and cannot wrap it in a Recorder; the bridge-boundary behaviour checks still run (G6) and the gate has no fake surface to compare (G7). G8.NO_UNIT x3 for ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed, the bridge-derived inputs the exemplar also leaves without units. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised; G1-G5 and G9 passed, and G6, G7 and G8 raised only the expected warnings.

NOT COVERED: the upstream 76-value observation vector (go2_mujoco_env.py:70), reward, curriculum, domain randomisation and rendering are not part of the cap.world.* contract served here; the state carries only time, qpos, qvel and ctrl. The upstream policy and the ROS2/Gazebo locomotion stack are not served. The parkour obstacles are parked at z -5 in the file and the parkour environment rewrites them at reset (go2_parkour_scene.xml:15-20); this driver serves the file as written. The real MuJoCo engine was never imported, so no trajectory was compared with it, and no physical Go2 is modelled or was validated.

LICENCE: the card pins license_spdx NOASSERTION and there is no top-level licence file. The README badge says MIT (README.md:6), training/setup.py declares BSD-3-Clause (training/setup.py:7) and ros2/LICENSE is a BSD-3-style text (ros2/LICENSE:1-6); the discrepancy is the card's needs_recon item and is recorded in facts.md. The package copies no upstream code or model file and reads the pinned model from the read-only clone.

No catalogue_requests: the package uses only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1. No operator_required limit and no site-limits overlay: the model file is the system of record for the control envelope. The upstream clone was not modified (G1 pass).
